tasks.title: Logback PAN masking + a test asserting it.
tasks.notes: Boot 4.1's structured logging bypasses Logback PatternLayout entirely - there is no %-converter to add. The real extension point, confirmed by decompiling spring-boot-4.1.1.jar with javap rather than trusting a summarized doc fetch: StructuredLoggingJsonMembersCustomizer, an SPI discovered via META-INF/spring.factories (documented in docs/spring-boot-4-notes.md). PanMasking (common-web) redacts any 12-19 digit run to its last four; PanMaskingJsonMembersCustomizer applies it across every String-valued member of the JSON envelope, not only "message", for every service that depends on common-web - not only card-service. PanNeverLoggedTest (card-service) both proves a real authorization never logs the PAN today AND deliberately logs one through the same real pipeline to prove the masking mechanism itself would catch a future leak, not merely current discipline. tasks.title: `analytics-service` scaffold, Flyway, consumers for ledger and card topics.
tasks.notes: analytics-service is this project's first pure read model. V3 lays down the phase's whole Design-detail schema up front (vault, transaction_category, monthly_spend, budget), verbatim, following ledger-service's scaffold precedent - none of the four are written to by this task, that is 06.2-06.6. V4 adds this task's own tables (ledger_entry_fact, card_authorization_fact) that its two consumers populate. LedgerEntryKafkaListener routes only EntryPostedV1 off ledger.entry.v1 - the one event that says money actually moved. CardAuthorizationKafkaListener routes AuthorizationApprovedV1/SettledV1/ReversedV1/ExpiredV1 off card.authorization.v1 - the full lifecycle of a hold that actually happened; AuthorizationDeclinedV1 is deliberately excluded (no hold placed, and a CARD_NOT_FOUND decline has no authorization id to key a row on), as are CardIssuedV1, AuthorizationRequestedV1 (full PAN, no userId) and simulator's own SettlementRequestedV1/ReversalRequestedV1 requests. Both handlers are upserts keyed on the event's own id with no side effect a redelivery could repeat, so neither is wrapped in an IdempotentHandler (same precedent as fx-service's LedgerAccountCreatedEventHandler); neither listener implements ConsumerSeekAware either, since unlike a small reference-data mapping this service's tables are the running transaction history - a full replay from offset zero is the phase's own separate `analytics-rebuild` operation, not something a listener does unprompted. Ambiguity resolved rather than guessed: EntryPostedV1 carries only a ledger account id, not a user id, and CLAUDE.md rule 7 forbids resolving that by reading another service's database, so ledger_entry_fact stores the ledger account id as-is and leaves that mapping for whichever later task needs it. Added two test classes (EntryPostedProjectionTest, CardAuthorizationProjectionTest) though none were named for this task, since the handler logic warranted more than a smoke test. GATE GREEN: mvn clean verify green from the repo root (23 files, +1374 lines), tripwire clean.

tasks.title: `monthly_spend` incremental upsert projection, bucketed on `occurredAt`.
tasks.notes: monthly_spend's write path plugs into AuthorizationSettledEventHandler (card.authorization.v1), not ledger.entry.v1: CardSettlementService posts CARD_SETTLEMENT entries with reference_id = null and correlates only via the ledger's own idempotency_key ("cardauth:<networkRef>"), which never reaches EntryPostedV1 - so there is still no clean ledger_entry_fact -> userId join (the same gap 06.1 already flagged). AuthorizationSettledV1 already carries userId and settledMinor/settledCurrency (wallet currency, not merchantSettledMinor/currency) directly, so monthly_spend is populated for card spend only for now; Transfers/Income/Cash (three of the phase's twelve categories) have no event source yet and are left for whichever later task solves the ledger account-to-user join - not invented here, per the task's own scope boundary. New: MonthlySpend/MonthlySpendRepository (a native ON CONFLICT upsert, the phase's own total_minor = total_minor + excluded.total_minor verbatim) and MonthlySpendProjectionHandler, which reads the category TransactionCategorisationService already assigned at approval time and buckets the month solely from the envelope's own occurredAt (UTC, first of month) - no Clock, no now() anywhere in the write path. AuthorizationSettledEventHandler's existing CardAuthorizationFact upsert stays unwrapped (naturally redelivery-safe); only the new monthly_spend increment is wrapped in an IdempotentHandler keyed on the envelope's eventId, since an incremental sum is not naturally safe against redelivery the way an upsert-by-key is. Checked card-service's SettlementService before assuming this was needed: settleable() requires state == APPROVED, so an authorization settles at most once (exact/partial/over-settlement all conclude it), and a reversal likewise only applies to an APPROVED authorization - so neither double-settlement nor reversal-after-settlement is reachable through the current settlement flow, and no delta-tracking beyond the IdempotentHandler guard was added; that edge case is left undocumented-but-deliberately-unhandled rather than guessed at, same house style as 06.1's own open gap. Tests: NoWallClockInProjectionTest (an event years old lands in its own historical month, not today's), MultiCurrencySpendTest (EUR and GBP spend in the same month/category stay as two separate rows), ProjectionRebuildTest (wipes monthly_spend/transaction_category/card_authorization_fact/processed_event and replays byte-identical envelopes -> identical aggregates, plus an extra redelivery-without-wipe case proving the guard alone stops double-counting). Found and worked around a real latent bug while writing ProjectionRebuildTest: ProcessedEvent.isNew() always returns true by design (so save() routes through persist(), which the dedup insert's constraint-violation detection depends on) - but that same override makes Spring Data JPA's plain deleteAll() silently skip every row when called via ProcessedEventRepository, since SimpleJpaRepository.delete(T) short-circuits and returns without deleting whenever isNew() is true. deleteAllInBatch() (a bulk JPQL DELETE that never consults isNew()) is the correct way to clear processed_event in a test - or in whatever Phase 07 builds for a real analytics-rebuild - documented at the call site rather than changed in common-messaging itself, since isNew()==true there is deliberate and shared by every other IdempotentHandler consumer in the codebase; worth a flag for whoever builds Phase 07's rebuild tooling. tasks.title: Retro-apply on user override, with aggregate correction.
tasks.notes: Hooked in at MerchantCategoryOverrideService.setOverride, inside the same transaction as the override write: new RetroApplyService.retroApply(userId, merchantName, newCategory) finds every CardAuthorizationFact this user has ever had with that merchant (CardAuthorizationFactRepository.findByUserIdAndMerchantNameIgnoreCase, case-insensitive to match MerchantCategoryOverrideRepository's own lookup) and, for each whose transaction_category.category differs from newCategory, calls TransactionCategory.retroApply(newCategory) (category + source=USER; assignedAt deliberately left untouched - it is the authorization's own event time, not the moment the user later corrected it) and, only if that authorization actually settled (settledMinor != null), corrects monthly_spend: MonthlySpendRepository.decrement (new - a plain UPDATE, not an upsert, since the bucket being reversed is guaranteed to already exist) on the old (userId, month, oldCategory, billingCurrency) bucket and the existing increment on the new one, using the identical month-bucketing (settledAt, UTC, first-of-month) and currency (billingCurrency) MonthlySpendProjectionHandler used when it first built the bucket - so the correction is the exact inverse/forward of the original write, not a re-derivation. An authorization already at the target category is skipped entirely (no write, no aggregate touch), which is also what makes setting the same override value twice a safe no-op for free. Scope decision - synchronous: implemented inline in the override-setting transaction rather than the phase's suggested async-event-plus-"updating..." UI, since there is no UI yet to show that state (Vaults/Analytics are tasks 06.9/06.10) and no test demands async behaviour; building an event + consumer + polling UI now would be speculative machinery ahead of an actual large-history perf problem. Documented as a deliberate, revisitable choice in RetroApplyService's own javadoc, not an oversight. Scope decision - idempotency: no explicit guard needed beyond the per-row "skip if already correct" check, since that alone makes a repeated identical override a true no-op (verified by settingTheSameOverrideValueTwiceIsASafeNoOp). RetroApplyTest (4 tests): the named scenario (MCC-derived Groceries authorization overridden to Shopping - transaction_category and both monthly_spend buckets corrected to the exact minor-unit amount), same-value idempotency, an approved-but-never-settled authorization (category corrected, no aggregate touched since no bucket ever existed), and an authorization already at the override's category (skipped entirely, assignedAt unchanged). Ambiguity resolved: the task left assignedAt's fate to my judgement since nothing tests it directly - chose to leave it as event time rather than bumping it to the override's action time, so it keeps recording when the underlying spend happened; merchant_category_override.updated_at already records when the user acted.
